symptom: The vacation and event availability sliders do not consistently match the legacy reference or the current supplier-backed API, and visible cards can change between reloads.
expected_behavior: Each tab uses the intended date window, displays only complete supplier-verified offers joined to published public businesses, and preserves the exact accepted API identity and order on every render.
environment: Legacy vii.co.il, public vii.spaplus.co API and local branch fix/reconcile-lost-features-20261102 on 2026-11-03.

steps: Open all five legacy vacation tabs and record date, business identity and price
Open all three legacy event tabs and record identity, availability text and price
Request all matching supplier-backed public API periods
Inspect the new vacation and event rail ordering code
reproduction.evidence: Legacy event tabs showed twelve claimed available venues but only two had prices; the current supplier API confirmed exactly those two complete event offers. Both new rail components applied document-seeded ordering after receiving the API response. Selected public catalog reads were capped at eight while the rail supports twenty.

observations.observation: The legacy site is not a safe current availability source after the same-day cutoff and marks event venues available without a verified price.
observations.evidence: Legacy last-minute tabs used 2026-11-03 after the current-day cutoff and ten of twelve event cards had no price; the current API returned two complete offers for 2026-11-04.

observations.observation: The new browser reshuffled already ordered API offers using a per-document seed.
observations.evidence: HomeLiveDeals and EventLastMinute called orderDiscoveryRail with useDocumentSeed after accepting the API payload.

observations.observation: The event API could select twenty offers but load public details for only eight identities.
observations.evidence: publicCatalogSelectedSummaries and readSupplierCatalogSelectedSummaries sliced requested IDs to eight.

observations.observation: The event hook stored results in a numeric-key object and did not retain the API result order.
observations.evidence: useViiLiveSearch exposed only results keyed by siteID before the repair.

hypotheses.mechanism: Client-side document-seeded ordering changes the accepted API order and makes the visible rail differ across page loads.
hypotheses.prediction: Identical API payloads can render different first cards when the document seed changes.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Inspect both components and render the same fixture through different seeds.
hypotheses.result: Both verified rail paths used the document seed; the new canonical boundary now ignores it and preserves input order.

hypotheses.mechanism: The eight-item selected-catalog cap silently drops valid event offers from a twenty-card rail.
hypotheses.prediction: More than eight complete offers can be present in results while at most eight matching public places are returned.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Trace includePlaces from offer selection through publicCatalogSelectedSummaries.
hypotheses.result: The API selected up to twenty IDs but both selected-summary layers truncated to eight.

hypotheses.mechanism: The legacy list is more complete and should be copied as current truth.
hypotheses.prediction: Every legacy claimed event venue has a complete current supplier offer.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare legacy identities and prices with the raw current supplier-backed API response.
hypotheses.result: Rejected: ten of twelve legacy cards lacked price, while the current API verified only the two complete priced offers.

fix.change: Preserve supplier API order at the browser boundary, retain explicit result order in the live-search hook, join event places in that same order, require complete event offers, remove unmatched offers, deduplicate identities, and raise selected-summary support to the rail limit of twenty.
fix.evidence: The focused slider, date-boundary, regional, catalog, event and vacation contract suites pass, including deterministic repeated-render and API-to-card identity tests.

affected_family: all vacation and event quick-date tabs

regression_checks.check: Identical API input preserves identical card identity and order
regression_checks.evidence: The canonical verified-slider helper test repeats the same fixture and asserts the exact same ordered identity list.

regression_checks.check: Duplicate or invalid identities are removed without reshuffling
regression_checks.evidence: The verified-slider helper test covers duplicate, empty and invalid identities while preserving the first accepted API occurrence.

regression_checks.check: Event results and public places have identical IDs and order
regression_checks.evidence: The event includePlaces route test asserts that offer identities and public place identities are equal and in the same order.

regression_checks.check: Only complete event offers with price date slot and room identity are displayed
regression_checks.evidence: The event route tests reject incomplete offers and accept only available positive-price offers with exact dates, slot and positive roomID.

regression_checks.check: All five vacation and three event date windows pass Israel time boundary tests
regression_checks.evidence: The deal-clock, regional availability and event slot suites pass every required preset and cutoff boundary.

regression_checks.check: Selected summary reads support twenty verified cards
regression_checks.evidence: Both selected catalog readers now cap at twenty, matching the rail contract, and the focused event projection tests pass.

remaining_unknowns: The legacy site does not expose enough evidence to distinguish stale availability from a different no-price business rule for its ten unpriced event cards; neither is safe to advertise as verified availability.
authorization_boundary: Diagnose, repair and verify locally; no supplier, CMS, database, secret, DNS or production publication mutation.
